summary: Security fix (Ed 2026-10-26). user_profiles granted every signed-in user (authenticated) INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, so a staffer could make themself admin, take the owner's email, or demote/delete the owner through the database API. Row level security may or may not already be on (production had it on, outside any migration). Ensures RLS is on, revokes all writes from authenticated/anon/PUBLIC, leaves authenticated SELECT limited to its own row. service_role (the server) and the 039 sign-in triggers keep working. No row changes.

preflight.name: user_profiles exists (548 works from either starting state: row level security on or off)
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'user_profiles' AND c.relkind = 'r'

preflight.name: the owner is the one and only active admin
preflight.sql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE role = 'admin' AND is_active AND lower(email) = 'egojara@bedrocktx.com'))::int * 10 + (count(*) FILTER (WHERE role = 'admin' AND is_active))::int FROM user_profiles

preflight.name: every profile's email matches its sign-in account (nothing already tampered)
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM user_profiles p JOIN auth.users u ON u.id = p.id WHERE lower(p.email) IS DISTINCT FROM lower(u.email)

preflight.name: auth.uid() exists (Supabase auth)
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'auth' AND p.proname = 'uid'

preflight.name: the 039 sign-in triggers are installed on auth.users
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = t.tgrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'auth' AND c.relname = 'users' AND t.tgname IN ('on_auth_user_created', 'on_auth_user_sign_in')

preflight.name: no policies on user_profiles other than the one 548 installs (548 would not remove an unknown policy; review any first)
preflight.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'user_profiles' AND policyname <> 'user_profiles_read_own'

expected_changes: user_profiles: row level security ensured ON (a no-op where it is already on); policy user_profiles_read_own (authenticated may SELECT only id = auth.uid()).
Privileges: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER revoked from authenticated, anon and PUBLIC; SELECT revoked from anon and PUBLIC. service_role keeps SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.
No row changes; no table, column, constraint, trigger or function changes.

verify.name: row level security is ON
verify.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'user_profiles' AND c.relrowsecurity

verify.name: signed-in users cannot insert, update or delete profiles
anon has no access at all
exactly one policy on user_profiles: the own-row read for authenticated
verify.sql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE policyname = 'user_profiles_read_own' AND cmd = 'SELECT' AND roles = '{authenticated}'::name[] AND qual = '(id = auth.uid())'))::int * 10 + count(*)::int FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'user_profiles'

verify.name: signed-in users keep SELECT (limited to their own row by the policy)
the owner is still the one and only active admin
verify.sql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE role = 'admin' AND is_active AND lower(email) = 'egojara@bedrocktx.com'))::int * 10 + (count(*) FILTER (WHERE role = 'admin' AND is_active))::int FROM user_profiles
